annotation.title_clean: Artificial intelligence in a digital age: European Parliament resolution of 3 May 2022 on artificial intelligence in a digital age (2020/2266(INI))
annotation.title_en: Artificial intelligence in a digital age: European Parliament resolution of 3 May 2022 on artificial intelligence in a digital age (2020/2266(INI))
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 465
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution adopting the AIDA Special Committee's report: six AI case studies and an EU Roadmap for global AI leadership. It urges a risk-based, technology-neutral regulatory framework, stronger data, skills, investment and sustainability policy, strict liability for high-risk AI, and meaningful human control and a ban on fully autonomous weapons.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports a risk-based, flexible, technology-neutral legal framework, with regulations preferred over directives for harmonisation.
High-risk AI should fall under strict liability with mandatory insurance; other AI harms under fault-based liability with presumption of fault.
High-risk AI should have stop buttons, logs, and human-in-the-loop oversight, and be subject to conformity assessment with CE marking.
Calls for a legally binding international instrument prohibiting fully autonomous weapons and ensuring meaningful human control.
Recommends regulatory sandboxes, EU standards, skills frameworks, investment, and green digital infrastructure to make the EU a global AI standard-setter.
